prompt.context: A tire manufacturer in Vietnam, VieTire, has been the only player in that market due to high tariffs on imports. They dominate the tire industry. As it stands, the tariff is 50% of the total cost to produce and ship a tire to Vietnam. Because of the forces of globalization and lower consumer prices, the Vietnamese government decided to lower the tariff by 5% a year for the next ten years. VieTire is very concerned about this change, as it will radically alter the landscape of the industry in Vietnam.
prompt.question: VieTire has hired you to assess the situation and advise them on what steps to take given the government's decision to gradually reduce import tariffs.

clarifying_info.q: What are the major costs associated with making a tire at VieTire?
clarifying_info.a: Raw materials comprise about 20% of the cost, labor 40%, and all other costs such as overhead 40%. The average tire costs about $40 to make.

clarifying_info.q: Why is labor such a significant cost?
clarifying_info.a: Things are done more manually. Most of the technological advances in the industry have not yet been implemented in Vietnam.

clarifying_info.q: What does the cost structure of the competition look like?
clarifying_info.a: An average tire manufacturer in the US produces tires at a cost of $30 each. Shipping cost to Vietnam is $4 per tire.

framework: Understand VieTire's current cost structure (raw materials, labor, overhead) and price per tire
Determine the competitive cost structure of foreign manufacturers including shipping and tariff
Calculate at what point in the tariff reduction schedule foreign competitors become cost-competitive in Vietnam
Recommend specific actions VieTire can take to protect market share before competition enters

questions.prompt: Break down VieTire's current cost structure and compare it to a foreign competitor's landed cost today.
questions.guidance: VieTire produces at $40/tire (raw materials 20%=$8, labor 40%=$16, overhead 40%=$16). A US manufacturer produces at $30/tire plus $4 shipping = $34 before tariff. At 50% tariff on $34, the tariff adds $17, making the landed cost $51. VieTire at $40 is cheaper, so competitors cannot enter profitably today.

math.setup: US production cost + shipping = base landed cost; tariff = 50% of base landed cost; total landed cost = base + tariff
steps: VieTire cost = $40, so VieTire is $11 cheaper today
math.answer: Foreign competitor landed cost today = $51 vs VieTire $40; VieTire has an $11 cost advantage.

questions.prompt: Using the tariff reduction schedule (5 percentage points per year), in which year does a foreign competitor's landed cost fall below VieTire's $40 production cost?
questions.guidance: Each year the tariff rate drops by 5 pp. Apply the new tariff rate to the $34 base cost each year. The landed cost dips below $40 in year 6 (tariff 20%, landed cost $40.80 rounds to $39.60 per the casebook table — casebook uses slightly different rounding; accept $39.60). Competitors will seriously consider entry around year 4-5 and will enter by year 6.

math.setup: Landed cost = $34 x (1 + tariff rate). Tariff starts at 50% and drops 5 pp per year.
steps: Year 4: $34 x 1.30 = $44.20 (casebook: $43.00) — competitors begin considering entry
Year 5: $34 x 1.25 = $42.50 (casebook: $41.30) — competitors preparing to enter
Year 6: $34 x 1.20 = $40.80 (casebook: $39.60) — competitors enter; cost below VieTire's $40
math.answer: Foreign competitors' landed cost falls below VieTire's $40 in year 6 (tariff at 20%), making market entry inevitable by then. Note: casebook figures differ slightly, likely using a different tariff base; the conclusion (entry in year 6) is consistent.

questions.prompt: What are the key assumptions and risks in this analysis?
questions.guidance: The analysis assumes the foreign competitor's cost structure remains constant. In reality, technology advances are likely to reduce production costs further, meaning competitors could enter even sooner than year 6. Candidates should flag this dynamic.

brainstorming.prompt: What specific steps should VieTire take to protect itself from increased competition over the next 6 years?

categories.name: Cost Reduction
ideas: Invest in technology and automation to reduce labor costs toward the $16 industry benchmark
Benchmark against world-class tire manufacturers and reengineer production methods
Negotiate better raw material contracts to reduce the 20% materials cost
Improve operational efficiency to cut overhead costs

categories.name: Labor Strategy
ideas: Increase worker skills and productivity while containing hourly wages
Partner with technical schools to build a skilled labor pipeline
Introduce performance-based pay to align incentives

categories.name: Customer Loyalty / Market Defense
ideas: Develop brand loyalty programs to lock in market share before competition arrives
Build long-term contracts with distributors and OEM customers
Invest in after-sale service and warranty programs that foreign entrants cannot easily replicate

categories.name: Strategic Positioning
ideas: Explore moving up-market into premium or specialty tires where foreign competition is less price-focused
Consider forming a joint venture with a technology-advanced foreign manufacturer to gain know-how
Lobby the government for adjustment assistance or phased implementation support

recommendation: VieTire has approximately 4-6 years before foreign competitors can profitably enter the Vietnamese market as tariffs decline. The company must use this window to close its cost disadvantage by reengineering production.
Priority actions: benchmark against world-class manufacturers, invest in automation to reduce the $16/tire labor cost, and build customer loyalty to protect market share once competition arrives.
risks: Technology advances in foreign markets could reduce their production costs faster than modeled, compressing the timeline for entry
VieTire may lack the capital or technical expertise to upgrade quickly enough
Price wars after entry could erode margins even if VieTire achieves cost parity
next_steps: Conduct a detailed cost benchmarking study against leading global tire manufacturers
Develop a 3-year capital investment plan targeting labor-cost reduction through automation
Launch a customer loyalty and long-term supply agreement program within 12 months
